findings.title: Backup-code login can skip password verification by also sending a dummy totpCode
findings.body: The password is only verified when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121, unchanged). The new branch at line 131 is chosen when `credentials.backupCode` is present, and it never looks at `totpCode`. An attacker can send `email` + any non-empty `totpCode` + a valid `backupCode`. The password check is skipped and the backup-code branch authenticates the request. A single secret (a 40-bit backup code) then replaces both password and second factor. The PR adds a new credential path on top of this guard without tightening it. Fix: always verify the password for CAL-provider users when no external TOTP/JWT flow is in progress, and make the backup-code branch independent of `totpCode`.

findings.title: Closing the dialog on the backup-codes step skips onEnable/resetState
findings.body: 2FA is already enabled server-side once the TOTP code is verified, but `onEnable()` and `resetState()` now run only from the "Close" button on the DisplayBackupCodes step. The Cancel button is hidden there. If the user dismisses the dialog via Escape, the overlay or the X (`onOpenChange`), the parent is never told 2FA was enabled, so the settings UI can still show it as off. The wizard also stays on `DisplayBackupCodes`, so reopening it shows stale codes. The user may never have saved the codes either. The dismiss path should be handled the same way as Close, or dismissal should be blocked on this step.

findings.title: "missing_backup_codes" message points to a settings feature that does not exist
findings.body: Users who enabled 2FA before this migration have `backupCodes = null`. When they click "Lost access" they get "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." There is no UI or endpoint to generate or regenerate backup codes for an already-enabled account. The only way to get codes is to disable 2FA, which requires a TOTP code or backup code they no longer have. The message gives an impossible instruction. Either add a regenerate flow or change the message to something actionable.

findings.title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: The code reads the encrypted blob, finds the index, nulls the entry, re-encrypts and writes the whole blob back, with no lock or compare-and-swap. Two concurrent logins using the same single-use code can both pass the `indexOf` check before either write lands. Both then succeed, violating the "can be used exactly once" guarantee. Concurrent logins using different codes can also overwrite each other's update and resurrect a used code. Use a transaction or optimistic concurrency, for example update where `backupCodes` equals the value that was read.

findings.title: Unvalidated backupCode type can crash the disable endpoint
findings.body: `req.body.backupCode` is only checked for truthiness, then `.replaceAll` is called on it. A non-string truthy value (number, object, array) throws a TypeError and returns a 500 instead of a 400 `IncorrectBackupCode`. Validate that it is a string before use, and ideally trim it.

findings.title: Empty backup code submit silently does nothing on the login form
findings.body: The login form uses `noValidate`, so the `required`/`minLength` attributes on the BackupCode input are not enforced. Submitting an empty backup code sends `backupCode: ""`, which is falsy. The server falls through to the TOTP branch and returns `SecondFactorRequired`. The handler then just calls `setTwoFactorRequired(true)` (already true), with no error shown. The user sees nothing happen. Handle the empty case client-side or show an error.

findings.title: No test coverage for logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code
findings.body: The core new behaviour is untested, and the PR checklist admits no tests were added. The e2e changes only click download/copy/close on the new screen, and the file/clipboard contents are TODOs. Nothing exercises backup-code login, one-time consumption of a code, disabling 2FA with a backup code, or the MissingBackupCodes/IncorrectBackupCode paths. The first test ("enable and login") never closes the new backup-codes dialog. Its `isChecked()` assertion is always truthy, as the FIXME admits, so it does not verify the new step. Given that this is authentication code, tests for the login and disable paths should be included.

findings.title: Copy button shows success toast without awaiting the clipboard write
findings.body: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` returns a promise that is neither awaited nor caught, and the success toast is shown immediately. If the write is rejected (permission denied, non-secure context, unfocused document), the user is told the codes were copied when they were not. For one-time recovery codes this is risky. Await the promise and show the toast only on success, with an error path otherwise.

findings.title: tabIndex={-1} on the shared password visibility toggle removes it from keyboard navigation
findings.body: This is a shared `PasswordField` used across the whole app, and the change makes the show/hide-password button unreachable by keyboard for every form. It is unrelated to backup codes and is an accessibility regression. If the goal was to improve tab order on the login or disable-2FA forms, apply it locally instead.
